chunks: And from him, from Ja'far ibn al-Muthanna al-Khatib, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl and Bashir ibn Isma'il, who said: Muhammad said to me, 'Shall I give you glad tidings, O son of Muthanna?' I said, 'Yes.' I stood up to him, and he said, 'This disbeliever/fiqh-opponent just entered and sat opposite Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him). Then he turned to him and said, 'O Abu al-Hasan, what do you say about the person in ihram? Does he seek shade under the saddle (mahmal)?' He said to him, 'No.' He said, 'Does he seek shade in the tent (khibah)?' He said to him, 'Yes.' He repeated the question to him in a mocking manner, laughing, 'O Abu al-Hasan, what is the difference between these two?' He said, 'O Abu Yusuf, indeed religion is not based on analogy (qiyas) like your analogy. You play [with the rules]. We did as the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did, and we said as the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would ride his mount, and he would not seek shade under it, and the sun would bother him, so he would cover part of his body with part [of his garment], and sometimes he would cover his face with his hand. And when he dismounted, he would seek shade in the tent, in the house, and by the wall.'

key_terms.الْخِبَاءُ: A tent or canopy used for shelter and shade
key_terms.الْقِيَاسُ: Analogical reasoning or deduction used in jurisprudence
key_terms.الْمَحْمَلُ: The saddle or covering on the back of a mount, often used for shade
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between a person in ihram seeking shade under their mount versus in a tent, according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of *tawqifi* (divine specification) over *qiyas* (analogical reasoning), as Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the specific prohibition of shade under the mount and the permissibility of shade in a tent. By referencing the Prophet’s (PBUH) actual practice of covering his body or face while riding versus using tents or walls when dismounted, the Imam establishes that ritual laws are based on transmitted tradition rather than logical deduction. This underscores the authority of the Ahl al-Bayt in preserving the precise details of Sunnah that might otherwise be lost to general analogical reasoning.
